newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BANKS' NET SOARS TO PLN 2.6 BLN IN H1.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BANKS' NET SOARS TO PLN 2.6 BLN IN H1.

text.p: The Polish banking sector's net profit increased by about 90 percent to 2.6 billion zlotys in the first six month of 1996, the central bank's General Inspectorate of Banking Supervision (GINB) said in a report.

The inspectorate's report released on Monday showed 72 commercial banks registered net profit while nine had losses in the first half of the year, compared with 69 and 19 respectively in the first quarter of the year.

The banks' gross profit was 3.6 billion in the first six months, a 62 percent rise compared with the same period of 1995. The banks paid taxes totalling 997 million zlotys, averaging 28 percent of profits earned.
The value of banks' total assets increased to 171.9 billion zlotys over the first six months, a 3.4 percent real growth or 15.2 percent nominal growth.
The banks' net own funds grew by a nominal 24 percent and a real 11.3 percent in the period.
The report showed foreign institutions controlled 22 commercial banks, and foreign capital accounted for 27.6 percent of the banking sector's total capital.
The report was based on information gathered from 81 commercial banks and 1,463 cooperative banks.
It did not take account of banks undergoing bankruptcy and in liquidation.
